title_en: Plan for the Restructuring of Arbitration Institutions

articles.content_en:
Article 5 An arbitration agreement shall exist independently; the modification, rescission, termination or invalidity of the contract shall not affect the validity of the arbitration agreement.
The arbitration tribunal shall have the power to confirm the validity of the contract.

Article 6 If a party challenges the validity of the arbitration agreement, it may request this Arbitration Commission to make a decision or request a People's Court to make a ruling. If one party requests this Arbitration Commission to make a decision and the other party requests a People's Court to make a ruling, the People's Court shall make the ruling.
A party that challenges the validity of the arbitration agreement shall raise the objection before the first hearing of the arbitration tribunal; if the parties agree not to hold a hearing, the objection shall be raised before the first submission of the statement of defense.
Article 8 The applicant applying for arbitration shall submit to this Arbitration Commission the arbitration agreement, the application for arbitration, and copies thereof.

Article 10 This Arbitration Commission shall, within 5 days from the date of receipt of the application for arbitration, accept the case if it considers that the conditions for acceptance are met, and shall notify the parties; it may also accept the case immediately and notify the parties. If it considers that the conditions for acceptance are not met, it shall notify the parties in writing of the rejection and state the reasons.
After receiving the application for arbitration, if this Arbitration Commission considers that the application does not comply with the provisions of Article 9 of these Provisional Rules, it may request the parties to make corrections within a specified time limit; if no corrections are made within the time limit, the application shall be deemed not to have been submitted.

Article 11 After accepting an application for arbitration, this Arbitration Commission shall, within 15 days, serve the applicant with these Provisional Rules and the list of arbitrators, and serve the respondent with a copy of the application for arbitration, these Provisional Rules and the list of arbitrators.
After receiving the copy of the application for arbitration, the respondent shall, within 15 days, submit a statement of defense to the Arbitration Commission. After receiving the statement of defense, the Arbitration Commission shall, within 15 days, serve a copy thereof on the applicant. The failure of the respondent to submit a statement of defense shall not affect the progress of the arbitration proceedings.

Article 12 The applicant may waive or modify the arbitration claim. The respondent may accept or reject the arbitration claim and shall have the right to file a counterclaim.
This Arbitration Commission shall, within 15 days from the date of receipt of the application for counterclaim filed by the respondent, serve a copy thereof on the applicant.
The applicant shall, within 15 days from the date of receipt of the application for counterclaim, submit a written defense to this Arbitration Commission; failure to submit a written defense shall not affect the progress of the arbitration proceedings.

Article 13 A party may apply for property preservation if, due to the conduct of the other party or for any other reason, it may be impossible or difficult to enforce the award.
If a party applies for property preservation, this Arbitration Commission shall submit the party's application to a People's Court in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Civil Procedure Law.
If the application is erroneous, the applicant shall compensate the respondent for any losses incurred as a result of the property preservation.

Article 14 A party or its statutory agent may appoint a lawyer or other agent to participate in the arbitration proceedings. If a lawyer or other agent is appointed, the party shall submit a power of attorney to this Arbitration Commission.
Article 15 The arbitration tribunal may be composed of three arbitrators or a sole arbitrator. If composed of three arbitrators, a presiding arbitrator shall be appointed.

Article 16 If the parties agree that the arbitration tribunal shall be composed of three arbitrators, each party shall select one arbitrator or entrust the Chairman of this Arbitration Commission to appoint one arbitrator, and the third arbitrator shall be selected jointly by the parties or jointly entrusted to the Chairman of this Arbitration Commission for appointment. The third arbitrator shall be the presiding arbitrator.
If the parties agree that the arbitration tribunal shall be composed of a sole arbitrator, the parties shall jointly select the arbitrator or jointly entrust the Chairman of this Arbitration Commission to appoint the arbitrator.

Article 17 If the parties fail to agree on the method of composition of the arbitration tribunal or to select the arbitrators within 15 days from the date of receipt of the notice of acceptance of arbitration, the Chairman of this Arbitration Commission shall make the appointment.

Article 18 After the arbitration tribunal is constituted, this Arbitration Commission shall, within 5 days from the date of constitution, notify the parties in writing of the composition of the arbitration tribunal; it may also notify the parties in writing on the date of constitution.

Article 20 A party applying for withdrawal shall state the reasons and shall file the application before the first hearing. If the ground for withdrawal becomes known after the first hearing, the application may be filed before the conclusion of the final hearing.

Article 21 The Chairman of this Arbitration Commission shall decide whether an arbitrator shall withdraw; if the Chairman of the Arbitration Commission serves as an arbitrator, the decision shall be made by the meeting of this Arbitration Commission.

Article 22 If an arbitrator is unable to perform his duties due to withdrawal or for any other reason, a substitute arbitrator shall be selected or appointed in accordance with the Arbitration Law and these Provisional Rules.
After the substitute arbitrator is selected or appointed due to withdrawal, a party may request that the arbitration proceedings already conducted be repeated; the arbitration tribunal shall decide whether to permit such repetition. The arbitration tribunal may also decide on its own whether to repeat the arbitration proceedings already conducted.

Article 23 If an arbitrator has a private meeting with a party or an agent, or accepts entertainment or gifts from a party or an agent, and the circumstances are serious, or if an arbitrator extorts or accepts bribes, engages in graft, or perverts the law in making an award in the arbitration of a case, the arbitrator shall bear legal liability according to law, and this Arbitration Commission shall remove his name from the list.

Article 24 Arbitration shall be conducted by holding a hearing. If the parties agree not to hold a hearing, the arbitration tribunal may render an award based on the application for arbitration, the statement of defense, and other materials.
Article 25 Arbitration shall not be conducted in public. If the parties agree to hold a public hearing, the arbitration may be conducted in public, except where state secrets are involved.

Article 26 The Arbitration Commission shall notify both parties of the date of the hearing at least 10 days before the hearing; with the consent of the arbitration tribunal, the parties may agree on an earlier hearing date. If a party has a legitimate reason, it may request a postponement of the hearing within 7 days before the hearing; the arbitration tribunal shall decide whether to postpone.

Article 27 If the applicant, after being notified in writing, fails to appear before the arbitration tribunal without justifiable reasons, or withdraws from the hearing without the permission of the arbitration tribunal, the application may be deemed to have been withdrawn.
If the respondent, after being notified in writing, fails to appear before the arbitration tribunal without justifiable reasons, or withdraws from the hearing without the permission of the arbitration tribunal, an award may be made by default.

Article 28 A party shall provide evidence to support its claims.
The arbitration tribunal may collect evidence on its own if it considers it necessary.

Article 29 Documentary evidence shall be submitted in the original. Physical evidence shall be submitted in the original. If it is truly difficult to submit the original or the original object, copies, photographs, duplicates, or excerpts may be submitted.
If documentary evidence in a foreign language is submitted, a Chinese translation shall be attached.

Article 1 These Interim Rules are formulated in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Arbitration Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Arbitration Law) and the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Civil Procedure Law) to ensure fair and timely arbitration of economic disputes and to protect the lawful rights and interests of the parties.

Article 2 Disputes over contracts and other disputes over property rights and interests between natural persons, legal persons and other organizations as equal subjects may be submitted to this Arbitration Commission for arbitration according to law.
This Arbitration Commission shall not accept arbitration applications arising from labor disputes and disputes over agricultural contracts within agricultural collective economic organizations.

Article 3 The parties shall resolve disputes through arbitration on a voluntary basis and reach an arbitration agreement. If there is no arbitration agreement and one party applies for arbitration, this Arbitration Commission shall not accept the case.

Article 5 An arbitration agreement shall exist independently; any modification, rescission, termination or invalidity of the contract shall not affect the validity of the arbitration agreement.
The arbitral tribunal shall have the power to determine the validity of the contract.

Article 6 A party who challenges the validity of an arbitration agreement may request this Arbitration Commission to make a decision or request a People's Court to make a ruling. If one party requests this Arbitration Commission to make a decision and the other party requests a People's Court to make a ruling, the People's Court shall make the ruling.
A challenge to the validity of an arbitration agreement shall be raised before the first hearing of the arbitral tribunal. If the parties have agreed not to hold a hearing, the challenge shall be raised before the first submission of the statement of defense.
Article 8 The applicant, when applying for arbitration, shall submit to this Arbitration Commission the arbitration agreement, the application for arbitration, and copies thereof.

Article 10 Within 5 days from receiving the application for arbitration, if this Arbitration Commission considers that the conditions for acceptance are met, it shall accept the case and notify the parties; it may also accept the case immediately and notify the parties. If it considers that the conditions for acceptance are not met, it shall notify the party in writing of the rejection and state the reasons.
After receiving the application for arbitration, if this Arbitration Commission considers that the application does not comply with the provisions of Article 9 of these Interim Rules, it may request the party to make corrections within a specified time limit; if the party fails to make corrections within that time limit, the application shall be deemed not to have been filed.

Article 11 After accepting an arbitration application, this Arbitration Commission shall, within 15 days, deliver these Interim Rules and the list of arbitrators to the applicant, and shall also deliver a copy of the application for arbitration, these Interim Rules, and the list of arbitrators to the respondent.
After receiving the copy of the application for arbitration, the respondent shall, within 15 days, submit a statement of defense to the Arbitration Commission. After receiving the statement of defense, the Arbitration Commission shall, within 15 days, deliver a copy of the statement of defense to the applicant. The failure of the respondent to submit a statement of defense shall not affect the conduct of the arbitration proceedings.

Article 12 The applicant may waive or amend the arbitration claim. The respondent may accept or reject the arbitration claim and has the right to file a counterclaim.
The Arbitration Commission shall, within 15 days from receiving the application for counterclaim filed by the respondent, deliver a copy of the application for counterclaim to the applicant.
The applicant shall submit a written defense to the Arbitration Commission within 15 days from receiving the application for counterclaim; the failure to submit a written defense shall not affect the conduct of the arbitration proceedings.

Article 13 If it may become impossible or difficult to enforce an award due to the conduct of one party or for any other reason, a party may apply for property preservation.
If a party applies for property preservation, this Arbitration Commission shall submit the party's application to the People's Court in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Civil Procedure Law.
If the application is erroneous, the applicant shall compensate the respondent for any losses incurred as a result of the property preservation.

Article 14 A party or a legal representative may appoint lawyers or other agents to participate in the arbitration proceedings. Where a lawyer or other agent is appointed to participate in the arbitration proceedings, a power of attorney shall be submitted to this Arbitration Commission.
Article 15 An arbitral tribunal may be composed of three arbitrators or a single arbitrator. Where it is composed of three arbitrators, a presiding arbitrator shall be appointed.

Article 16 If the parties agree that the arbitral tribunal shall be composed of three arbitrators, they shall each select or each entrust the Chairman of this Arbitration Commission to appoint one arbitrator. The third arbitrator shall be selected jointly by the parties or jointly entrusted to the Chairman of this Arbitration Commission for appointment. The third arbitrator shall be the presiding arbitrator.
If the parties agree that the arbitral tribunal shall be composed of a single arbitrator, the parties shall jointly select or jointly entrust the Chairman of this Arbitration Commission to appoint the arbitrator.

Article 17 If within 15 days from receiving the notice of acceptance of arbitration, the parties fail to agree on the method of composition of the arbitral tribunal or fail to select the arbitrators, the Chairman of this Arbitration Commission shall make the appointments.

Article 18 After the arbitral tribunal is formed, this Arbitration Commission shall, within 5 days from the date of formation, notify the parties in writing of the composition of the arbitral tribunal; it may also notify the parties in writing on the day the arbitral tribunal is formed.

Article 20 A party who applies for the withdrawal of an arbitrator shall state the reasons and shall submit the application before the first hearing. If the grounds for withdrawal become known after the first hearing, the application may be submitted before the conclusion of the last hearing.

Article 21 Whether an arbitrator shall withdraw shall be decided by the Chairman of this Arbitration Commission; if the Chairman of the Arbitration Commission acts as an arbitrator, the decision shall be made by the meeting of this Arbitration Commission.

Article 22 If an arbitrator is unable to perform his or her duties due to withdrawal or for any other reason, a substitute arbitrator shall be selected or appointed in accordance with the Arbitration Law and these Interim Rules.
After a substitute arbitrator is selected or appointed due to withdrawal, the parties may request that the arbitration proceedings already conducted be repeated; whether to grant such request shall be decided by the arbitral tribunal. The arbitral tribunal may also decide on its own motion whether the proceedings already conducted shall be repeated.

Article 23 If an arbitrator privately meets a party or an agent or accepts hospitality from a party or an agent, and the circumstances are serious, or if an arbitrator, in arbitrating a case, extorts or accepts bribes, engages in favoritism or malpractice, or renders an award in perversion of law, he or she shall bear legal liability according to law, and this Arbitration Commission shall remove his or her name from the panel.

Article 24 Arbitration shall be conducted by holding hearings. If the parties agree not to hold hearings, the arbitral tribunal may render an award on the basis of the application for arbitration, the statement of defense, and other materials.
Article 25 Arbitration shall not be conducted in public. If the parties agree to public hearing, the arbitration may be conducted in public, except where state secrets are involved.

Article 26 The Arbitration Commission shall, 10 days before the hearing date, notify the parties of the date of the hearing. Upon agreement of both parties and with the consent of the arbitral tribunal, the hearing may be held earlier. If a party has a legitimate reason, it may request an adjournment of the hearing within 7 days before the hearing; whether to adjourn the hearing shall be decided by the arbitral tribunal.

Article 27 If the applicant, having been notified in writing, fails to appear before the arbitral tribunal without justifiable reasons or leaves the tribunal without the permission of the arbitral tribunal, the application for arbitration may be deemed withdrawn.
If the respondent, having been notified in writing, fails to appear before the arbitral tribunal without justifiable reasons or leaves the tribunal without the permission of the arbitral tribunal, an award may be made by default.

Article 28 A party shall provide evidence for its own claims.
If the arbitral tribunal considers that it is necessary to collect evidence, it may collect the evidence on its own initiative.

Article 29 Documentary evidence shall be submitted in original form. Physical evidence shall be submitted in its original object. If it is indeed difficult to submit the original document or object, reproductions, photographs, copies, or extracts may be submitted.
If documentary evidence in a foreign language is submitted, a Chinese translation shall be attached.

Article 30 If the arbitral tribunal deems it necessary to conduct an expert evaluation on a specialized issue, it may refer the matter to an expert evaluation department agreed upon by the parties, or to an expert evaluation department designated by the arbitral tribunal.
Upon the request of a party or at the request of the arbitral tribunal, the expert evaluation department shall assign an expert to attend the hearing. A party may, with the permission of the arbitral tribunal, put questions to the expert.
Article 31 Evidence shall be presented at the hearing, and the parties may cross-examine each other's evidence.

Article 32 Where evidence is likely to be destroyed or difficult to obtain later, a party may apply for preservation of evidence. If a party applies for preservation of evidence, this arbitration commission shall submit the party's application to the Primary People's Court in the place where the evidence is located.

Article 33 The parties shall have the right to debate during the arbitration proceedings. At the conclusion of the debate, the presiding arbitrator or the sole arbitrator shall solicit the final opinions of the parties.

Article 34 The arbitral tribunal shall record the hearing in the minutes. If a party or any other participant in the arbitration considers that there is an omission or error in the record of its own statement, it shall have the right to apply for a correction; if the correction is not made, the application shall be recorded.
The minutes shall be signed or sealed by the arbitrators, the recorder, the parties, and other participants in the arbitration.

Article 35 After applying for arbitration, the parties may settle the dispute amicably on their own. If a settlement agreement is reached, they may request the arbitral tribunal to render an arbitral award based on the settlement agreement, or they may withdraw the arbitration application.
Article 36 If a party reneges after reaching a settlement agreement and withdrawing the arbitration application, it may apply for arbitration in accordance with the arbitration agreement.

Article 37 Before rendering an award, the arbitral tribunal may first attempt mediation. If the parties voluntarily agree to mediation, the arbitral tribunal shall conduct mediation. If mediation fails, the arbitral tribunal shall render an award promptly.
If a mediation agreement is reached, the arbitral tribunal shall prepare a mediation statement or render an arbitral award based on the terms of the settlement. The mediation statement and the arbitral award shall have equal legal effect.

Article 38 The mediation statement shall state the arbitration claims and the terms agreed upon by the parties. The mediation statement shall be signed by the arbitrators, sealed with the seal of this arbitration commission, and served on both parties.
The mediation statement shall take legal effect after being signed for receipt by both parties.
If a party repudiates the mediation statement before signing for receipt, the arbitral tribunal shall render an award promptly.

Article 39 The award shall be made in accordance with the opinion of the majority of the arbitrators. The dissenting opinion of a minority of the arbitrators may be recorded in the minutes. If the arbitral tribunal is unable to form a majority opinion, the award shall be made in accordance with the opinion of the presiding arbitrator.
Article 40 When arbitrating a dispute, if part of the facts have been ascertained, the arbitral tribunal may make an interim award on that part.

Article 41 The arbitral tribunal shall render an arbitral award within four months after its formation. If an extension is necessary due to special circumstances, the presiding arbitrator or the sole arbitrator may, with the approval of the director of this arbitration commission, appropriately extend the time limit.

Article 42 The arbitral award shall state the arbitration claims, the facts of the dispute, the reasons for the award, the result of the award, the allocation of arbitration costs, and the date of the award.
If the parties agree not to state the facts of the dispute and the reasons for the award, they may be omitted.
The arbitral award shall be signed by the arbitrators. An arbitrator who disagrees with the award may sign or not sign the award.
Article 43 After the arbitral award is signed by the arbitrators, the arbitration commission shall affix the seal of this arbitration commission.
Article 44 The arbitral award shall take legal effect from the date on which it is made.

Article 45 The arbitral tribunal shall correct any clerical or computational errors in the award or any matters that were adjudicated by the arbitral tribunal but omitted from the award; a party may, within 30 days from receipt of the award, request the arbitral tribunal to make such corrections.

Article 47 A party shall perform the award within the time limit specified in the arbitral award. If no time limit is specified, the party shall perform the award immediately.
If one party fails to perform the arbitral award, the other party may apply to the People's Court for enforcement in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Civil Procedure Law.

Article 48 If the law has provisions on the time limit for arbitration, such provisions shall apply; if the law has no provisions on the time limit for arbitration, the provisions on the limitation of action shall apply.

Article 49 Unless otherwise agreed by the parties or otherwise required by the arbitral tribunal, arbitration documents, notices, and materials may be served directly on the parties or their representatives, or may be served by mail, fax, telegram, or other means.

Article 50 Time periods shall be calculated by the hour, day, month, or year. The hour or day from which a time period begins shall not be counted as within the time period.
If the last day of a time period falls on a holiday, the day following the holiday shall be deemed as the last day of the time period.
The time period shall not include time in transit; if arbitration documents, materials, or notices are posted or sent before the expiration of the period, they shall not be deemed as overdue.

Article 51 If a party fails to meet a time limit due to force majeure or other justifiable reasons, it may apply for an extension within 10 days after the removal of the obstacle; whether to grant the extension shall be decided by this arbitration commission or the arbitral tribunal.

Article 52 The remuneration of an arbitrator shall be determined by this arbitration commission based on factors such as the working hours of the arbitrator in handling the arbitration case, the complexity of the case, and the amount in dispute.
The remuneration of an arbitrator shall be paid from the case acceptance fees collected by this arbitration commission.
Article 53 These Interim Rules shall take effect as of [ ] year [ ] month [ ] day.
